top_choice_rationale: Katori and Ye for the optical lattice clock rests on one specific mechanism, magic-wavelength trapping, that removes the trade-off between atom number and Doppler, recoil and collision shifts. It has been reproduced at the 1e-18 level by several independent laboratories, with systematics that atomic-structure theory explains. It already yields physics (millimetre-scale gravitational redshift, bounds on drifting constants, many-body effects in the clock), and the two-name allocation is clean. The citation must name the lattice scheme and the 1e-18 regime so it stays distinct from the 2005 comb and 2012 ion-control prizes. IceCube (P002) is a real discovery but the three-name allocation from a large collaboration is a judgement call and source identification is still incomplete, and I defer to colleagues on astroparticle physics. Both are preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; no direct link to the lattice-clock or IceCube candidates (my own field is superconducting circuits, and the AMO and astroparticle fields lie outside it)
